The Sewing Products portfolio spans household straight-stitch, artisan, zigzag, embroidery (single and multi-needle) and industrial sewing machines and related accessories, while the Home Appliances portfolio spans room coolers, irons, heaters, washing machines and kitchen appliances, along with an extensive fan range. building a stronger, more resilient ecosystem that supports localisation and improves supply chain agility|Modernise the sewing ecosystem and accelerate a sewing and creator mindset transformation through product innovation, customer education and stronger engagement across distribution, retail and owned social media channels|Strengthen the portfolio across domestic and industrial sewing machines while expanding presence in premium and high-potential categories (e.g. Link Motion technology introduced in the Black straight-stitch machine)|Invest in experiential retail formats, Sewing Studios and community/workshop-led engagement to reposition SINGER as a modern and aspirational brand and support premiumisation|Deepen digital capabilities across commerce, marketing and customer service, with e-commerce treated as an important growth driver supported by investment in digital visibility and online engagement|Portfolio diversification beyond sewing into small appliances and fans, where premiumisation trends are seen as an encouraging opportunity|Recalibrate channel mix, optimise the product portfolio and strengthen the e-commerce strategy to build a more resilient business through the cyclical home-appliance downturn|Drive sustainable profitability through disciplined cost control, supply chain efficiency, channel productivity, product pricing and sharper portfolio management|Continue investments in innovation, manufacturing capabilities and digital transformation while enhancing operational efficiencies, expanding adoption of AI-enabled capabilities and strengthening governance frameworks|Strengthen quality systems and integrate customer feedback across the product lifecycle to improve product reliability and service readiness|CSR focused on women empowerment and livelihood generation through sewing and entrepreneurship-led skill development, including the 'Ek Nayi Pehchaan' initiative|The Company returns cash to shareholders through an annual dividend recommended by the Board and approved by members at the AGM. For FY 2025-26 the Board, at its meeting held on 27 May 2026, recommended a final dividend of Rs. 0.40 per equity share of Rs. 2 each, placed as an ordinary resolution before the 48th AGM. No formal dividend distribution policy, buyback, debt-reduction plan, credit rating or explicit reinvestment philosophy is described in the sections provided. Governance framework: the Board comprises eight directors - one Executive, three Non-Executive Independent and four Non-Executive Non-Independent (including one Woman Director) - with a Non-Executive Independent Chairperson, four Board meetings held during the year with no gap exceeding 120 days, and no inter-se relationship between directors.|Certified as a Great Place to Work for the third consecutive year, reflecting sustained focus on employee engagement and workplace excellence|Stated commitment to building a diverse workforce with a continued focus on increasing women's representation across departments, supported by unbiased and inclusive hiring practices and a structured onboarding process|Continuous learning and development programmes conducted to bridge skill gaps, enhance employee capabilities and improve retention|Internal control system with quarterly internal audits carried out by a firm of Chartered Accountants to protect assets, ensure transactions are approved and recorded correctly and reduce the chance of fraud
currentContext.expansion: Manufacturing and localisation: during FY 2025-26 the Company commenced production of its first Made-in-India Auto Zig Zag machines from its Jammu facility, strengthening its localisation and manufacturing capabilities under the 'Make in India' initiative, alongside its highest-ever sales in the Auto Zig Zag category. The Company describes continued investment in the sewing machine and home appliances segments for portfolio expansion, and states that with a strong and skilled R&D team it is ready to lead the manufacturing industry in the modern sewing machine segment; new technologically advanced products introduced include DSBB and SLBB sewing machines, a straight-stitch machine with Link Motion technology (both winners of the 15th CII Design Excellence Awards in Best Product Design), single-needle and multi-needle embroidery machines, and Tailor Mate, a motorised straight-stitch machine positioned against traditional cast-iron machines. Retail and channel build-out: the Company is redesigning its experiential retail footprint through dedicated Experience Centres designed to transform consumer engagement through interactive demonstrations and product education, with the newly redesigned retail store in Hosur cited as a step towards stronger brand visibility and premium positioning; it also continues to expand e-commerce and digital-first initiatives to enhance omnichannel capabilities. Distribution and service footprint comprises over 10,000 sales points, 6,400+ dealers and distributors, and an after-sales service network covering over 7,000 pin codes, complemented by the 'SINGER Live Assist' digital support platform through which over 20% of customer complaints are resolved. In home appliances and fans, expansion is product-led - premium and newer offerings such as Steam Station, Blenders, Induction Cooktops and Infrared cooktops, and a fan portfolio spanning recently launched BLDC fans, Induction fans, TPW and Decorative fans - with strengthened distribution and after-sales service capabilities. No rupee capex plan, commissioning schedule or capacity number for any site is disclosed in the sections provided.
currentContext.mdna: India is entering a new phase of sewing machine adoption, with consumers gradually transitioning from conventional cast iron machines toward modern zigzag, electronic and feature-rich machines; low penetration of modern machines in one of the world's largest sewing machine markets is seen as a substantial category-expansion opportunity|The Sewing Machines segment continues to benefit from favourable structural trends, including increased government focus on artisan livelihoods, growth in garment manufacturing and rising consumer preference for feature-rich products|The Home Appliances segment is navigating a near-term demand moderation driven by unfavourable weather conditions, higher commodity cost increases and elevated channel inventories - management sees these challenges as largely cyclical|The Fans segment maintained steady growth through new products such as energy-efficient BLDC and decorative fans alongside better channel reach, despite soft market demand and pricing pressure from new BEE rating transitions|Overall profitability continued to be influenced by the share of institutional and government business, which typically operates at lower margins, even as margin improvement was visible across several product categories and distribution channels|Volatility in currency (forex) prices and supply chains during the year prompted intensified efforts on supply chain efficiency, channel productivity and disciplined cost control|Sewing demand is supported by growing interest in creativity, DIY sewing, skill enhancement and home-based entrepreneurship; the Home ZigZag and Artisan segments benefit from rising participation among hobbyists, learners and skilled users|A vibrant digital creator ecosystem around sewing, embroidery, quilting and DIY craft content across Instagram, YouTube and other platforms is attracting new users to the category|India's apparel manufacturing sector is projected to grow by approximately 10.5% in FY 2026, supported by rising exports, domestic consumption and government support (PLI scheme for textiles, PM MITRA parks, ~USD 595 million Cotton Mission investment)|The Indian sewing machine market (household, artisan and industrial) is estimated at approximately Rs. 3,000 Crore and is projected to witness 4-6% growth year on year across key segments|PM Vishwakarma Yojana and state-level Free Silai Machine schemes are boosting both supply and demand, with most state-funded schemes requiring 'Made in India' equipment - creating bulk-order opportunities for domestic manufacturers|Mandatory BIS certification and evolving quality control frameworks are expected to strengthen industry formalisation and favour organised players with strong compliance and manufacturing capabilities|The Indian home appliances market is projected to expand at a CAGR of 5.70% during 2026-2035, supported by premiumisation, energy efficiency, connected/intelligent home ecosystems and Tier II/III and rural penetration|India's textile exports crossed Rs. 3.16 lakh crore in FY2025-26 with export growth across more than 120 destinations, and global sourcing diversification is creating a favourable long-term environment for the industry|Key headwinds flagged: competition from low-cost unorganised players and imports in price-sensitive markets, volatility in steel, component and electronic input prices, labour shortages and wage pressure, and global tariff-related disruptions

risks.risk: Intense competition from unorganised players and low-cost imports
risks.note: Competition from unorganised players and low-cost imported products may impact revenue growth, particularly in price-sensitive markets; the Company mitigates through value-engineered products, brand communication via advertising and social media, and leveraging Quality Control Orders (QCO) to restrict low-quality imports.

Exchange rate volatility may affect financial performance given imported sourcing; managed through appropriate hedging activities in line with internal policies. The MD's message notes the year witnessed volatility in currency (forex) prices and supply chains.

Increasing raw material prices may impact cost structures and profitability; the Company is implementing cost reduction measures through design optimisation and exploring alternative cost-efficient suppliers.

risks.risk: Market demand fluctuations / changing consumer preferences
risks.note: Changes in consumer preferences may affect product demand; mitigated by continuous analysis of market trends and adapting product offerings to evolving consumer needs. Home appliance demand was noted as subdued during the year.

Unforeseen events may disrupt the operational efficiency of the organisation; the Company has established comprehensive risk management policies and regularly reviews risk exposure to develop appropriate action plans.

External cyberattacks may disrupt business operations and compromise systems; firewalls, threat monitoring systems with real-time response, access controls over critical IT systems and data protection policies are deployed.

Failure of customers to meet contractual obligations may result in financial loss; mitigated by monitoring customer creditworthiness, setting credit limits and applying expected credit loss models to assess impairment. Relevant given the dealer/distributor and institutional sales model.

Non-compliance with applicable laws and regulations may result in legal penalties; compliance is ensured through regular audits and periodic reviews. The industry also faces evolving BIS certification, BEE rating and quality control requirements that raise certification and product development costs.

thesis (one-liner): Asset-light heritage brand gaining clear market share in a slow-growing (~4–6%) sewing-machine market via new products, dealer engagement and e-commerce leadership; strong sewing momentum (Rev +29% FY26, EBITDA +70%) masks a still-loss-making appliances/fan build-out; Bhiwadi factory + ZigZag/Industrial indigenization is the multi-year optionality, funded by ~Rs.83cr net cash.
scorecard: One-offs (explicit): FY26 includes a one-time exceptional cost of Rs. 73 lakhs from the change in the labour code. Adjusted: EBITDA Rs. 22.2 cr (+76%), PBT Rs. 18.1 cr (+80%). Appliances segment result was ~Rs. 2 cr lower mainly due to EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility) impact + investment in building Fan business.
guidance (critical): No explicit revenue/margin guidance given. Mgmt repeatedly declined to commit to numbers ("I will not be able to comment exactly on future profits").
Sewing growth momentum described as sustainable ("reasonably confident we can sustain this growth momentum") — built on market-share gains, not one-offs.
Business mix expected to stay ~75–80% sewing / 20–25% appliances; no dramatic shift in 1–2 years; growth ambitions "equal in both categories."
Appliances/fans: confident it "is going to be a very profitable business"; declined to commit to Q1 FY27 break-even.

PMY govt order: >60% supplied, ~40% balance; expected to complete "before the beginning of the second half" (i.e., by H1 FY27 / ~Sept 2026, revised slower than earlier June-2026 target due to allocation pace). A second PMY order expected but timing govt-dependent.
Capex: up to Rs. 90 cr over 3 years (Bhiwadi, phased; not yet committed).
demand / pipeline: Sewing demand strong across ALL channels: Govt (PMY), Retail/Trade, E-commerce.
Industry growing only ~4–6%; Singer's outperformance = market-share gains.

Headwinds in Q4: geopolitical-driven commodity-price spike, labour shortage in parts of country (textile hubs like Tirupur/Surat cited), supply shortages, blocked trade inventory (esp. appliances), tight dealer cash flows.
Appliances demand muted on unfavorable weather + blocked inventory; fans picking up with heatwave.
segment (sewing vs appliances): Sewing Machines (~81% of revenue):
Category Rev: ~+45% Q4, +40%+ FY26. Trade channel +~20% Q4, +15%+ FY26.
ZigZag (future of household): +30%+. Industrial: +13% Q4, +20%+ FY26. Cast-iron straight-stitch + accessories +50%+ FY26.
New machines (DSBB, SLBB, Link) ~15% of household sewing category.
E-commerce: +50%+ Q4, ~+30% FY26; #1 in sewing on e-commerce.
Company sewing mix (FY): ZigZag ~20%, classic Black ~55%, Industrial+accessories ~28–30%.
Total India sewing market ~Rs. 3,000 cr (industrial ~55% / ~Rs.700cr straight-stitch household / ~Rs.350cr artisan / ~Rs.250cr zigzag).
Appliances (~19% of revenue):
Rev ~+10% Q4, but segment result ~Rs. 2 cr lower (EPR + fan investment).
Fans ~+50% Q4; full range launched (Economy/Base/Decorative/BLDC/TPW/Exhaust); new distributors onboarding.
Steaminator (premium steam iron) gaining traction; exhaust fans well received on e-commerce.
growth / optionality: Indigenization (Make-in-India) of ZigZag + Industrial sewing machines — large under-penetrated categories vs global; bridging price gap to drive household ZigZag adoption.
New Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) leased factory — production H2 FY27; primarily ZigZag, also Industrial + select appliances.
Already commenced ZigZag assembly in India; new full-aluminium-body heavy-duty ZigZag made at Jammu factory.
Tailor Mate (motorized lightweight straight-stitch at cast-iron price point) — modernization optionality replacing obsolete black machines.
Fan business build-out; e-commerce-first product strategy.
Experience Centres expanding (Nehru Place store won ET Award for Design & Creativity).
margins & cost: Commodity inflation a major headwind; PMY orders are fixed-price — increases must be absorbed (no pass-through to govt).
Mgmt expects operating leverage + indigenization to aid margins as scale builds ("It is very logical").
ROCE ~10% (improved YoY); investor pushed back that 10% is sub-par.
capex: Up to Rs. 90 cr over 3 years (Bhiwadi), phased and not yet firmly committed.
Strategy: start lean — leased factory, assembly first, components outsourced; in-house critical components later. "3-year journey."
capital allocation: ~Rs. 83 cr cash on books (broadly unchanged since 2023).
Resumed dividend: Rs. 0.40/share — framed as signaling a "profitable journey ahead" (back on dividend list).
Investor pressed for a large one-time special dividend to lift ROCE; mgmt declined, intends to deploy cash into "positive opportunities" / catapult organization to new level; "noted."
~Rs. 7 cr in >1yr FDs with Yes Bank (non-current); Rs. 11.6 cr intangible = SVP manufacturing rights (Nov-2025, amortized >24 yrs).
risks: Promoter (Retail Holdings India BV) exit overhang — mgmt would "neither confirm nor deny" M&A/sellout; recurring stock overhang.
Fixed-price PMY orders + commodity inflation = margin squeeze; PMY allocation pace slowing/lumpy; dependence on govt order flow.
Low ROCE (~10%) + large idle cash (capital-efficiency criticism).
management tone: Confident and growth-oriented on sewing ("strong momentum," "sustainable"); cautiously optimistic on appliances ("challenges temporary," "very profitable business" but won't commit to break-even). Guarded/evasive on promoter-exit and capital-return questions. Emphasized Make-in-India and market-share narrative; humble on macro ("I have not seen the future").
non-obvious insights: Q4 was NOT the usual seasonal "big bang" — Q3 (~Rs.160cr) ≈ Q4 (~Rs.166cr); mgmt reframes this as a higher sustainable run-rate rather than weakness.
PMY timeline quietly slipped from June→~Sept 2026 due to slower govt allocations — first hint of order lumpiness.
E-commerce-first design is becoming the lever for appliances (reducing reliance on high-cost modern trade).
~50% of Indian sewing market revenue already from high-speed machines (Juki competition acknowledged in industrial).
Acquired SVP manufacturing rights (Rs.11.6cr) — supports indigenization thesis.
challenges → beneficiaries: ⭐ Make-in-India / import substitution in ZigZag + Industrial sewing machines positions Singer as a domestic beneficiary vs imports (China/Juki).
✅ Heatwave / fan demand tailwind into Q1 FY27.
(Promoter exit, PMY fixed-price margin pressure = challenges with no clear listed beneficiary.)
qoq log: Q4 FY26 (this call): Rev Rs.166.3cr (+37% YoY); FY26 Rev Rs.557cr (+29%), EBITDA Rs.21.5cr (+70% reported / Rs.22.2cr +76% adj), PBT Rs.17.3cr (+73% reported / Rs.18.1cr +80% adj). One-off: labour-code Rs.73L. Sewing +45% Q4, e-com +50% Q4 (#1). Appliances rev +10% but result -Rs.2cr (EPR + fan invest). Fans +50% Q4. PMY >60% done. Cash ~Rs.83cr; div Rs.0.40 resumed; ROCE ~10%. Capex up to Rs.90cr/3yr (Bhiwadi). NSE listing done. Promoter-exit Q dodged.
(Prior quarters: no earlier transcripts in this batch — establish baseline from this note.)

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.
themes.driver: Summer cooling demand; GST 2.0 price cuts; festive restocking; commodity-cost tailwind on margins; premiumization/ASP mix shift.
